UI_TOOLKIND_QUERY_MODEL: Simulates a small condition grammar. Observe whether your input is used only as a value or changes the query's structure (for example an OR condition). With parameter binding on, input is treated only as a value.
UI_TOOLKIND_QUERY_LIMIT: Does not reproduce a real SQL engine or its full grammar. Only in-game virtual rows are involved; no real database is contacted.
UI_TOOLKIND_RENDER_MODEL: Compare whether input is shown only as text or interpreted as a virtual display signal. With escaping on, it is shown only as text.
UI_TOOLKIND_RENDER_LIMIT: No real JavaScript runs. Effects on other users are computed only as fixed virtual outcomes.
UI_TOOLKIND_PATH_MODEL: Appends your input to the base path, normalizes it, and shows whether the result leaves the public area. With the boundary policy on, paths outside are refused.
UI_TOOLKIND_PATH_LIMIT: Normalization happens only inside the virtual file system. No real OS path or file is accessed.
UI_TOOLKIND_EXEC_MODEL: Observe whether input stays a single argument of a registered virtual job or appends another job through a separator. With argument arrays on, appended jobs are ignored.
UI_TOOLKIND_EXEC_LIMIT: No real process or shell runs. Only a fixed list of virtual jobs exists.
UI_TOOLKIND_FETCH_MODEL: See how the acting party and reachable range change when the server requests an address on your behalf. With the egress policy on, internal addresses are blocked.
UI_TOOLKIND_FETCH_LIMIT: Only in-game .test addresses are involved; there is no real internet request. Reaching an internal host does not mean admin rights.
UI_TOOLKIND_PERMISSION_MODEL: Check how the current session account relates to an exposed group name. Group rights only matter in that account's session.
UI_TOOLKIND_PERMISSION_LIMIT: No real account, sudo or OS permission is changed. Only virtual groups in the game world are involved.
UI_TOOLKIND_AUDIT_MODEL: Decode the provided virtual bytes with the XOR key and compare them with the stored value. You type the decoded string yourself.
UI_TOOLKIND_AUDIT_LIMIT: No real hash cracking or external wordlists. XOR here is an example of a simple transform, not protection.
UI_TOOLKIND_REVERSE_MODEL: Follow the transform a program applies to the given bytes (here XOR) and compute the result.
UI_TOOLKIND_REVERSE_LIMIT: No real executable is analyzed or run. Only a small transform model is involved.
UI_TOOLKIND_MEMORY_MODEL: Shows a fixed-size buffer and the cells after it. Write hex bytes to see which cell any overflowing byte reaches.
UI_TOOLKIND_MEMORY_LIMIT: Does not reproduce real process memory, addresses or mitigations. Only a bounded set of virtual cells is involved.
UI_TOOLKIND_PACKET_MODEL: Pick virtual packet rows seen at an observation point with a field=value filter to find the related flow.
UI_TOOLKIND_PACKET_LIMIT: No real network is captured. It only models the principle that encrypted segments do not reveal their body to an on-path observer.
UI_TOOLKIND_TRACE_MODEL: Pick log and route records with field=value to link traces of the same incident.
UI_TOOLKIND_TRACE_LIMIT: No real system log is read. Uncertainty such as clock skew or gaps is only as complete as the case records.
UI_TOOLKIND_COMPARE_MODEL: Put two observed values side by side and confirm what the specific difference is.
UI_TOOLKIND_COMPARE_LIMIT: It confirms a difference; it does not decide the cause for you.
UI_TOOLKIND_TOKEN_MODEL: Check whether a fictional token found during the investigation is a currently approved value.
UI_TOOLKIND_TOKEN_LIMIT: No real credential or service token is used. A deleted setting may still need its past value's effect checked separately.
UI_TOOLKIND_POLICY_MODEL: Apply one allowed policy value, then the case goals and current service state are evaluated again. By default false is the vulnerable behavior and true is the blocking behavior.
UI_TOOLKIND_POLICY_LIMIT: Goals separately check that normal features still work after a change. Blocking everything is not the answer.
UI_TOOLKIND_IDOR_MODEL: Request an object number as the currently authenticated account and see how the owner-check policy changes the response.
UI_TOOLKIND_IDOR_LIMIT: Only a virtual object list is involved. Real authorization designs vary far more.
UI_TOOLKIND_AUTH_MODEL: Counts failures per account and a virtual wait. With the limit policy on, observe both the block after repeated failures and a normal sign-in after waiting.
UI_TOOLKIND_AUTH_LIMIT: No real time passes; waiting uses a logical clock in ticks. This is not a real brute-force tool.
UI_TOOLKIND_SESSION_MODEL: Issue, reuse, revoke and wait with session tokens, and check that revoked or stale tokens are refused while a fresh one is accepted.
UI_TOOLKIND_SESSION_LIMIT: Clearing a cookie on screen is not the same as server-side revocation. This model computes server-side state only.
UI_TOOLKIND_CSRF_MODEL: See whether state-changing requests check origin and token, so forged requests are blocked while legitimate changes still succeed.
UI_TOOLKIND_CSRF_LIMIT: Real browser cookie policies are not reproduced. An authenticated virtual session is required.
UI_TOOLKIND_UPLOAD_MODEL: Observe whether file extension, MIME type and signature agree, and whether a stored file becomes executable. Check both that bad files are refused and normal photos are accepted.
UI_TOOLKIND_UPLOAD_LIMIT: No real file is received or executed. Only name, type and signature are modeled.
UI_TOOLKIND_SCAN_MODEL: From the selected terminal's current position, check whether the target's ports look open, closed or filtered. Same handling as the nmap command.
UI_TOOLKIND_SCAN_LIMIT: An open port is not access. Results change when the starting point changes. No real network is scanned.
UI_TOOLKIND_ROUTE_MODEL: From the selected terminal's current position, see which hops lead to the target. Same handling as the traceroute command.
UI_TOOLKIND_ROUTE_LIMIT: Only the in-game virtual network graph is involved. Being able to reach a host is not the same as having rights on it.
UI_TOOLKIND_FILE_MODEL: Reads a file with the selected terminal session's account rights. It passes the same permission checks as cat.
UI_TOOLKIND_FILE_LIMIT: Only the virtual file system is involved. Without permission, reading through a tool is refused too.
UI_TOOLKIND_LOG_MODEL: Reads a log file with the selected terminal session's rights so you can compare times, actors and targets yourself.
UI_TOOLKIND_LOG_LIMIT: Logs only say what was recorded. Do not settle a conclusion on an empty record or matching timestamps alone.

UI_HELP_BODY:
This computer is a virtual terminal inside the game. Servers, sites, files and tools are all fictional; nothing reaches a real network, shell or web browser.

Windows
  Drag the title bar to move · double-click or □ to maximize/restore · drag the bottom-right corner to resize
  ─ minimize · × close: hides the window only; sessions, input and history are kept
  Ctrl/Cmd+1–9: Terminal · Mail · Browser · RequestLab · Tools · Files · Evidence · Case board · Status
  Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+1–4: Terminals 1–4 · Ctrl/Cmd+Tab: switch window
  F1 help · F6 taskbar · Shift+F6 top bar text size and pause · F10 back to studio
  Esc outside a text field: pause

Terminals
  Terminals 1–4 share one world but each keeps its own connection, working directory, command history and password prompt.
  Enter runs · ↑/↓ history · Tab completes · Esc clears input or cancels a password prompt · Ctrl+L or clear wipes the screen
  Passwords are hidden and never recorded. exit and Disconnect close only that terminal's remote connection.

Browser and RequestLab
  Only in-game virtual addresses open. The browser, curl and RequestLab share one virtual request handler.
  RequestLab headers and body must be JSON objects; malformed input is not sent.

Tools
  Tools are not answer buttons. Read the published observations, enter a hypothesis and compare results.
  Empty input is never sent. Advanced JSON input is optional. Which tool you used never decides a case.

Case board and hints
  Shows the real status of the current goals. Hints open only when you ask, in order 1 → 2 → 3.
  When every goal is met you can move to the next case. Switching cases keeps each case's state.

Saving
  Progress is saved automatically when the state changes. If saving fails, autosave pauses and you choose between restoring the backup or keeping damaged files and saving new.
  Evidence pins, comparisons and notes are screen aids only; they are not saved or used to decide a case.

Alerts
  Alerts rise only for refused actions the server observed. Local typos, reading, switching windows and time passing never raise them.
